what_happened: Launched deploy-headless.sh in the background and continued editing Phase 4's source files (runtime-file-patterns.sh, the standards doc) before it finished. The deployed tree captured a partial edit state, causing test-runtime-file-tracking.sh (which resolves .claude/ before the source store) to see a stale 20-member lib paired with a stale standards doc and fail Case 5. Also surfaced an unrelated pre-existing specs/TODO.md sync drift from task 329's own earlier IMPLEMENTING status transition not yet regenerated into TODO.md.

scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh has 14 pre-existing failures (Group 28/Arm B-D) unrelated to this task, caused by a missing generate-task-order.sh in the test fixture's scratch .claude/scripts/ copy (ERROR: generate-task-order.sh failed with exit code 127). Confirmed pre-existing by re-running the identical suite against the unmodified git-HEAD copy of orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (same 335 passed/14 failed split), so this task's Phase 6 edits are not the cause. Not fixed here -- out of this task's scope -- but recorded so a future reader does not misattribute it.

The full repo test sweep (scripts/tests/run-all.sh) flags 5 failing suites, 3 already tracked as EXPECTED by run-all.sh's own baseline (test-gate-out-repair-reporting.sh, test-lint-json-channel-discipline.sh, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) and 2 flagged NEW (test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, test-typst-element-lint.sh). Verified zero file-level overlap between this task's touched files and any of the 5 failing suites' own test files or their SUTs (git log over this task's commit range returns no hits for any of them), and for test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh specifically confirmed by direct comparison that the unmodified git-HEAD copy fails identically. None of these 5 are regressions from this task; the NEW classification for 2 of them is a pre-existing baseline-tracking gap, not something this task introduced.

scripts/update-phase-status.sh's heading-status replacement uses a GREEDY sed pattern (line ~322: sed -i "${line_number}s/\[.*\]/[${new_status}]/"). When a phase's own title contains a literal square-bracket pair (this plan's Phase 7: 'Record the `errors[]` Verdict and Retire `reflection` in Core'), the greedy [.*] match spans from the FIRST '[' in the title (inside `errors[]`) through the LAST ']' on the line (the status bracket), destroying everything in between. The heading corrupted from '### Phase 7: Record the `errors[]` Verdict and Retire `reflection` in Core [NOT STARTED]' to '### Phase 7: Record the `errors[COMPLETED]', silently losing the phase's own title text. Caught only by eye during a post-Phase-9 review of all nine phase headings; fixed manually by restoring the correct title text. A one-line fix (anchor the pattern to the trailing bracket group, e.g. s/\[[^][]*\]$/[...]/ or anchor with $ and a non-greedy/bracket-exclusion character class) would prevent recurrence for any future plan phase whose title contains inline-code square brackets.
